title: Patch: the perf check times the combat forecast that every host computes beside each view
thread:
**Issue #4472 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4472: Patch: the perf check times the combat forecast that every host computes beside each view
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Each time the board changes, the game works out what every attack you could make would do: the preview a player sees before attacking. It does this for each player, on the server and, in practice games, in the player's browser. The repository's speed check times most of the engine's work but not this preview. A change that made it ten times slower would pass every check and show up only as a slower board. Once this is built, the daily speed check also times the preview and fails when it slows past its budget.

## Why

- **What it costs.** `combat_forecast` (`crates/engine/src/query.rs:1140`) runs `legal_actions`, then forecasts every listed attack. For each attack with a destroying hit on a board whose layers read the board, `forecast_attack`'s `settle_deaths` (`query.rs:1474`) clones the whole `GameState` (R4379000).
- **Recent growth.** That clone landed on 2026-11-21 (#4379, commit 0cd6b9dfb3), the day after `perf.rs`'s budgets were measured (2026-11-20, `crates/tools/src/perf.rs:73`).
- **Every host calls it with each view:**
  - the server's match actor (`crates/server/src/actor/engine.rs:144`), sent as R3477000's `forecast` beside the view (`actor/protocol.rs:227`);
  - daily games (`crates/server/src/daily/games.rs:603`);
  - the practice host on every snapshot, in the browser's WebAssembly (`crates/shared/src/host/practice/host.rs:605`);
  - the duel and Duos hosts (`crates/shared/src/host/duel.rs:538`, `duos.rs:810`, once per seat);
  - the WebAssembly export (`crates/wasm/core/src/lib.rs:417`).
- **What perf times today.** `cargo jackioh perf` times `reduce`, `view_for`, `legal_actions`, `hash_state`, the folds and their Duos versions, and `view_for`'s bytes (`MEASURES` in `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs`). It never times the forecast.
- **Measured for this survey,** with a scratch program outside the repo (the engine and the cards, release build without the workspace's thin LTO) on 2,507 states of 60 random-policy games:
  - the forecast cost 0.22 times `view_for` at the median and 0.61 times at the 95th percentile;
  - on the 27 states listing 10 or more attacks, its median was 3.5 ms and its worst 20.9 ms.
- **The existing check passes.** `target/release/jackioh perf` on the same 4-core machine took 21 s, and all ten measures were within their release budgets (`view_for` median 338.9 µs, p95 4,496 µs over its 78 states).

## Proposal

- **Two new measures** in `perf.rs`, timed in each pass beside `view_for`:
  - `combat_forecast`: each seat on each 1v1 corpus state;
  - `duos_combat_forecast`: each seat's duel on each Duos state, as `duos.rs` calls it.
- **Budgets.** Each gets a median budget at both profiles (`COMBAT_FORECAST_US_BUDGET_TEST` and `_RELEASE`, and the Duos pair), measured the way `perf.rs:73-79` says: three runs of each profile, 5 times the largest median, rounded up to two significant figures. Each constant's doc comment gives its three medians.
- **Reporting.** The table, `--json` and `MEASURES` in `tests/perf.rs` gain both rows.
  - The daily `perf_holds_every_budget` judges them.
  - `--smoke` times them in its one pass and judges only the work budget, as today.
  - The table's header line also counts the forecast's listed attacks, so a corpus that lists none is visible.
- **Docs.** The `perf` row of `crates/tools/README.md` names the new measures.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/perf.rs`, `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs` and `crates/tools/README.md`.
- SPEC: R3100000 and R3477000 (the forecast, and the hosts sending it), §9.9 (the perf gate's place beside the AI's).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `jackioh perf` and `jackioh perf --json` print `combat_forecast` and `duos_combat_forecast` rows with median, p95 and budget, and `tests/perf.rs`'s `MEASURES` lists them.
- [ ] `every_measure_over_its_budget_fails_naming_its_median_p95_and_budget` covers the two new measures: a median over budget fails, naming the constant.
- [ ] A test shows the corpus holds at least one state whose forecast lists 10 or more attacks. If none does, the pull request adds one, for example from the AI gate's wide boards.
- [ ] The four budget constants carry the three medians of each profile that set them, measured as `perf.rs:73-79` says.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf` passes, and so does the daily `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf perf_holds_every_budget -- --ignored`.

## Size and risks

Small: about 80 lines and four constants in one module and its test, medium difficulty.

- **Coarse guard.** At 5 times headroom, the budget catches a large slowdown, not a 20% drift. That is how every other measure here is held.
- **Native only.** It times the native build, not the browser's WebAssembly, as the other measures do.
- **Longer runs.** The daily perf test grows by about the forecast's share of `view_for`'s time, and the per-pull-request smoke grows by one more pass of it, a few seconds.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

## Plan

_Written by `gpt` (codex, `gpt-5.6-sol`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45042592793)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Extend `cargo jackioh perf` so every timed pass measures `combat_forecast` for both seats of every 1v1 corpus state and for every Duos seat's underlying duel, and report both rows in the table and JSON with calibrated test/release median budgets. Make the report expose the listed-attack coverage, including proof that one corpus forecast has at least 10 attacks, while preserving `--smoke`'s work-budget-only verdict and documenting the expanded command.

## Files to touch

| Path | Kind | Changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` | change | Add the two forecast measures, samples, four calibrated budgets, attack-count reporting, table coverage, and unit-test fixture updates. |
| `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs` | change | Expand `MEASURES` and make `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once` prove forecast rows and a 10-attack corpus state. |
| `crates/tools/README.md` | change | Update the `perf` command row with both forecast timings, attack counts, and twelve measures. |

Do not touch `crates/engine`, `crates/shared`, any server or app, any spec/ruling note, or `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, or `.claude/`. The behavior is governed by SPEC §9.9, R3100000 (forecast contents/public-board-only semantics), R3477000 (hosts send forecasts with views, including Duos filtering), and R4379000 (state-check settlement cost); this instrumentation makes no new rules decision, so it needs no ruling.

## Steps

1. In `crates/tools/src/perf.rs`, update the module documentation and engine imports: import `combat_forecast`; say a pass times it beside `view_for` for each 1v1 seat and on `&state.duels[seat.duel()]`/`seat.player()` for each Duos seat; change the count of clocked timings from nine to eleven. Preserve the existing deterministic corpus and warmup/pass behavior.
2. In the budgets block of `crates/tools/src/perf.rs`, add `COMBAT_FORECAST_US_BUDGET_TEST` after the test-profile `view_for` constant, `COMBAT_FORECAST_US_BUDGET_RELEASE` after the release `view_for` constant, and `DUOS_COMBAT_FORECAST_US_BUDGET_TEST`/`DUOS_COMBAT_FORECAST_US_BUDGET_RELEASE` beside the corresponding Duos `view_for` constants. Adjust the block's lead comment so its 2026-11-20 date clearly describes the existing budgets and the new forecast constants are documented as the later calibration using the same runner and procedure. To collect the first measurements, use finite compile-only placeholder values of `1.0`; after instrumentation is complete, run three test-profile and three release-profile measurements as step 8 describes, then replace every placeholder. Each final value is exactly five times the largest of its row's three medians, rounded upward to two significant figures; each doc comment must list those three observed medians and say `5x headroom`, matching the existing constants' format. Do not alter or remeasure the existing budgets.
3. Extend `Measure` in `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` with `CombatForecast` immediately after `ViewFor` and `DuosCombatForecast` immediately after `DuosViewFor`; grow `MEASURES` from 10 to 12 in that same order. Map them in `Measure::name` to `combat_forecast` and `duos_combat_forecast`, in `unit` to `us`, in `needs_clock` to `true`, and in `budget` to the profile-appropriate constants and their exact constant-name strings. This makes the existing `every_measure_over_its_budget_fails_naming_its_median_p95_and_budget`, at-budget, and smoke-verdict unit tests cover both rows without special cases.
4. Split the existing timer helper into `seconds_with_result<T>`, which returns `(elapsed_seconds, black_boxed_result)`, and `seconds<T>`, which delegates to it and drops the result as today. Add `combat_forecast: Vec<f64>`, `duos_combat_forecast: Vec<f64>`, `forecast_attacks: usize`, `max_forecast_attacks: usize`, and `duos_forecast_attacks: usize` to `Samples`; in `Samples::extend`, extend both vectors, add each total, and keep the larger maximum. In `timed_pass`, immediately after each `view_for`, use `seconds_with_result` on `combat_forecast(state, seat)`, push its elapsed microseconds, add its `attacks.len()` to the 1v1 total, and update the maximum. Do the same immediately after each `duos_view_for` with `combat_forecast(&state.duels[seat.duel()], seat.player())` and the Duos total. This counts the exact timed results without an extra forecast pass. Do not reuse the separately computed legal-action lists: production `combat_forecast` performs its own `legal_actions` call, which is part of the cost this measure is intended to catch. Do not include `DuosHost::forecast`'s later retain/filter pass; this row measures the raw engine call the host invokes.
5. In `measure`, add both timing vectors to the `MEASURES` extraction match. Add `forecast_attacks`, `max_forecast_attacks`, and `duos_forecast_attacks` as `usize` fields of `CorpusCounts`, serialized by the existing rename as `forecastAttacks`, `maxForecastAttacks`, and `duosForecastAttacks`. Because `Samples::extend` sees the deterministic counts once per timed pass, report each total divided by `passes` and report the maximum unchanged. Totals make a zero-work corpus visible for each row; the per-call maximum, rather than an aggregate, proves the acceptance threshold. Warmup samples remain dropped, and `--smoke` still invokes exactly one timed pass.
6. Extend `perf_table`'s first line in `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` with `forecast: {forecast_attacks} attacks (max {max_forecast_attacks}); duos forecast: {duos_forecast_attacks} attacks`. Increase the measure-column padding in both the table header and row formats from 18 to at least 21 so `duos_combat_forecast` does not crowd its unit. In `the_table_has_a_line_per_measure_under_its_header`, initialize the three new `CorpusCounts` fields with distinct fixture values and assert the first line contains all three; its existing `MEASURES`-driven assertions must now cover twelve rows.
7. In `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs`, grow its `MEASURES` constant to 12 names in exactly the source report order, inserting `combat_forecast` after `view_for` and `duos_combat_forecast` after `duos_view_for`. In `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once`, assert both forecast totals are numeric (zero remains reportable), define a local named threshold constant with value 10, and assert `corpus["maxForecastAttacks"]` meets it. Keep the generic per-row assertions, which prove both new JSON rows have samples, median, p95, and budget; keep `perf_holds_every_budget`'s body and daily ignore reason intact.
8. Calibrate the four constants only after all rows and report coverage compile. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf perf_holds_every_budget -- --ignored` three separate times and record each `combat_forecast` and `duos_combat_forecast` median from the printed table; the temporary low budgets may make these calibration runs exit nonzero, but their tables remain the measurement evidence. Then run `cargo build --release -p jackioh-tools` once and `target/release/jackioh perf` three separate times, recording the same two rows. For each profile/measure let `x = 5 * max(three medians)`, `scale = 10^(floor(log10(x)) - 1)`, and the budget be `ceil(x / scale) * scale`; write that exact upward-two-significant-figure value to the matching constant and replace its comment with the three medians. Rerun both profile commands after the final values and require success.
9. In the `perf [--smoke] [--json]` row of `crates/tools/README.md`, say each 1v1 seat's `combat_forecast` and each Duos seat's underlying-duel forecast are timed beside their views, the header/JSON report the listed-attack totals and maximum, and the daily test judges all twelve rows. Retain the explanation that `--smoke` times one pass but judges only the deterministic `view_for bytes` work budget.

## Tests

- `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` — existing `every_measure_over_its_budget_fails_naming_its_median_p95_and_budget` must iterate all twelve measures and verify the two new over-budget messages include median, p95, value, unit, and the appropriate `*_TEST` or `*_RELEASE` constant name. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-tools every_measure_over_its_budget_fails_naming_its_median_p95_and_budget`.
- `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` — existing `the_table_has_a_line_per_measure_under_its_header` must verify twelve aligned rows and the 1v1 total/maximum and Duos total in the header. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-tools the_table_has_a_line_per_measure_under_its_header`.
- `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs` — `perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once` must verify the exact twelve-row JSON order, valid statistics/budgets for both forecast rows, attack-count fields, and `maxForecastAttacks >= 10`. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf perf_smoke_times_the_corpus_once`.
- Run the complete targeted integration test with `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf`.
- Run the final test-profile budget gate with `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf perf_holds_every_budget -- --ignored` and the final release gate with `target/release/jackioh perf` after `cargo build --release -p jackioh-tools`.
- Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `cargo jackioh patches check`, and `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] Table and `--json` output contain `combat_forecast` and `duos_combat_forecast` rows with samples, median, p95, and profile budget.
- [ ] Both attack totals and the single-forecast maximum appear in the summary/JSON, and the smoke test proves a corpus forecast lists at least 10 attacks.
- [ ] The four new constants contain 5x-upward-rounded budgets and comments with the three measured medians for their exact profile.
- [ ] The generic over-budget test covers and names both new measures and their constants.
- [ ] `--smoke` times the new clocked rows but still judges only `view_for bytes`; the daily run judges all twelve rows.
- [ ] The tools README accurately describes the expanded measurement and report.
- [ ] Targeted tools tests, both final profile budget runs, rustfmt, tools clippy, catalog, patches, and spec checks pass.
- [ ] `git diff --check` is clean and only the three planned files are tracked as changed.

## Risks

- Forecast cost depends strongly on attack count and board-reading layers. Reporting separate totals plus the maximum prevents a cheap or empty corpus from making a healthy median meaningless; the fixed corpus keeps comparisons deterministic.
- `combat_forecast` intentionally calls `legal_actions` internally. Reusing the already timed list would measure a different implementation and hide the production cost; call the exported function whole and keep the earlier `legal_actions` timing separate.
- Duos exposes fewer attacks than an underlying duel and filters after the engine forecast. Time the underlying raw call for each seat, as the host does, and count that raw result; do not change Duos filtering or include shared-host code in this patch.
- Shared-runner timing is noisy. Use exactly three runs per profile, the largest median, upward two-significant-figure rounding, and 5x headroom; never derive a budget from p95 or the survey's scratch figures.
- Both new rows are clocked. Marking either unclocked would make the one-pass smoke gate flaky; keep `view_for bytes` as the only smoke-judged row.
- Calling the existing forecast changes no state, replay, hash, client contract, or hidden-information boundary (R3100000). No engine, host, spec, or wire type should change.

## Open questions

None. The four numeric budgets and comment medians are deliberately produced by the prescribed six calibration runs rather than guessed in the plan; the rounding rule makes their final values mechanical.
```
